comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C37, C38, C66 regarding curvature dominance over elevation. Both evaluations find the wall experiment design compelling and accept the conclusion that curvature is the dominant cue, though OpenEval notes the 64% success rate while peer reviewers accept the design without questioning this limitation.

Perfect agreement on claims C61, C66 regarding methodological innovations. Both evaluations praise the use of unmarked pellets and the experimental design separating collection from deposition. Peer reviewer explicitly calls the experiments 'ingenious' while OpenEval describes them as 'well-justified.'

Strong agreement on claims C71-C79 regarding biological plausibility of humidity sensing. Both evaluations accept the physiological evidence and sensory capabilities of termites. OpenEval provides detailed analysis of the supporting citations while peer reviewers implicitly accept this reasoning without critique.

Strong agreement on claims C69, C103-C105 regarding reconciliation with previous literature. Both evaluations explicitly praise this contribution. Editor states findings 'reconcile discrepancies between previous studies' and anonymous reviewer notes work 'possibly unifies the different hypothesis presented in the last 8 years.'

Strong agreement on claims C86, C87, C89, C94 regarding pheromone independence. Both evaluations accept that pheromones are not necessary for early deposition site selection. Peer reviewers note the use of 'loose and unmarked pellets' while OpenEval emphasizes the experimental design and simulation support.

Strong agreement on main conclusions C8, C9, C109, C110 (plus C38, C40 in peer review). Both evaluations find the evidence 'compelling' and accept the curvature-evaporation mechanism. Editor and anonymous reviewer both affirm the claims are well-justified, with peer reviewer calling it 'the best attempt on characterizing multiple cues.'

Agreement on claims C4, C29, C32, C62, C63 regarding spatial separation of collection and deposition. Peer review also includes C5, C30, C33, C64, C65 (covered separately by OpenEval R2 and R3). Both evaluations strongly support these findings, with peer reviewers describing experiments as 'ingenious' and evidence as 'compelling.'

Partial overlap on deposition patterns (C5, C30, C33, C64). OpenEval R2 focuses specifically on concentrated deposition at pillar tips and disk edges, while peer R1 groups these with collection behavior claims. Both evaluations strongly support the experimental observations.

Minimal overlap on claim C65 regarding conditional probability analysis. OpenEval R3 specifically addresses the quantitative evidence from P(D|O) and P(C|O) analysis, while peer R1 includes this claim within broader support for spatial patterns. Both find the evidence supportive.

Agreement on claims C6, C51-C53 regarding chemical garden experiments and evaporation hypothesis. Peer review also includes C7, C48, C50, C68. Peer reviewer specifically praises chemical garden as 'very ingenious low tech solution' while OpenEval notes the correlational nature and appropriate use of speculative language.

Agreement on claims C7, C48, C68 regarding curvature-evaporation proportionality. Peer review groups these with broader evaporation claims (C6, C50-C53). Both evaluations accept the analytical derivation and experimental validation, with peer reviewers finding evidence 'compelling.'

Minimal overlap on claim C50 regarding disk edge deposition explanation. OpenEval R11 specifically addresses the coffee stain analogy and humidity gradient simulations, while peer R2 groups this with general evaporation findings. Both find the reasoning sound.

Agreement on claims C46, C47 regarding diffusive regime assumptions. Peer review also includes C44, C45 on environmental measurements. Peer reviewer initially felt humidity measurements were missing but accepted the alternative approach. OpenEval emphasizes the theoretical justification through literature and scaling.

Agreement on claims C44, C45 regarding temperature and humidity measurements. Peer review also includes C46, C47. Both evaluations accept the environmental characterization, with peer reviewer noting initial concern about missing humidity probes but accepting the chemical garden alternative.

Agreement on claim C39 regarding simulation validation. OpenEval R5 also includes C40. Both evaluations accept the qualitative agreement between experiments and simulations. Peer reviewer praises the use of 'expertise of numerical simulations' while OpenEval notes appropriate acknowledgment of limitations.
Minimal overlap on claim C40 regarding curvature sufficiency. OpenEval R5 focuses on simulation agreement while peer R3 emphasizes overall mechanistic conclusions. Both find the evidence supportive.

Partial agreement on broader implications (C118-C120). OpenEval finds claims C117-C120 appropriately supported by citations to analogous systems, rating them SUPPORTED. Peer review finds this context initially insufficient, rating UNCERTAIN, noting authors 'do not discuss how their results affect our understanding' broadly enough, though improvements were made in revision.

Minimal overlap on claim C85 regarding humidity discrimination capabilities. OpenEval R14 specifically analyzes the scaling argument for sensory plausibility, while peer R8 implicitly accepts biological plausibility without detailed discussion. Both support the claims.

Minimal overlap on claim C88 regarding simulation support for pheromone independence. OpenEval R15 focuses on pheromone-related claims while peer R5 emphasizes simulation methodology. Both accept the simulation results as supporting evidence.

OpenEval R12 addresses claims C54, C55, C57-C59 regarding variability in deposition patterns and weaker gradients. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers did not specifically comment on variability explanations.

OpenEval R16 rates claims C90-C93 as UNCERTAIN, noting appropriate speculation about natural conditions and pheromone roles in other contexts. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers did not specifically address these limitations.

OpenEval R18 addresses claims C99-C102 regarding robustness to porosity and roughness through scaling analyses. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers did not specifically comment on these theoretical robustness arguments.
